subtitle: From Abyssinian Bondman to the Shadow on Jahangir’s Throne

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Malik Ambar on horseback atop a Deccan ridge, Mughal banners distant on the horizon, stormy sky above
panels.action: Malik Ambar sits tall on a dark horse at the edge of a rocky Deccan plateau, wind whipping his turban as distant Mughal standards line the horizon below.

dialogue.text: Born a stolen boy from Ethiopia, Malik Ambar rose to command kings and defy emperors in the burning plains of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: इथियोपिया से अगवा हुआ मलिक अंबर, दक्खन की आग में राजाओं का सेनापति बना, सम्राटों को ललकारता हुआ।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the Ethiopian highlands and Red Sea coast, fading toward the Arabian Sea
panels.action: A sweeping view of rugged Ethiopian hills slopes down toward a crowded Red Sea port, with dhows anchored and caravans edging toward the water.

dialogue.text: Around 1548, in the highlands of Ethiopia, a boy named Chapu took his first breath, unaware that the sea below would carry him into bondage.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1548, इथियोपिया के पहाड़ों में चापू नाम के लड़के ने पहली सांस ली, अनजान कि नीचे का समुंदर उसे ग़ुलामी में बहा ले जाएगा।

panels.shot: tight mid-shot on the deck of a dhow, chained African youths, Arab merchants in the background, sea stretching vast
panels.action: On the creaking deck of a wooden dhow, African youths sit bound in rows as robed merchants look on and the sun blazes on the Arabian Sea.

dialogue.text: The Futuhat-i Adil Shahi speaks of Chapu sold into the Islamic Indian Ocean slave trade, shipped through Yemen and the Red Sea like cargo.

i18n.hi: फ़ुतुहात-ए आदिलशाही में लिखा है कैसे चापू को हिंद-ओसियानी ग़ुलाम बाज़ार में बेचा गया, यमन और लाल सागर के रास्ते माल की तरह ढोया गया।

panels.shot: tracking mid-shot through a street in Yemen or Mecca, madrasas and markets, with a young African boy in simple robes among scholars
panels.action: In a bustling West Asian street lined with arches and madrasas, a young African boy in plain robes walks beside a scholar, clutching a slate.

dialogue.text: Sold, converted and renamed, the boy learned Arabic letters and law in Yemen and Mecca, his mind honed even as his freedom was denied.

i18n.hi: बेचा गया, धर्म बदला, नाम बदला, पर यमन और मक्का में उसी ने अरबी इल्म और क़ानून सीखा, दिमाग तेज़ होता गया, चाहे जान उसकी क़ैद रही।

panels.shot: wide of a busy port like Mocha with ships bound for India, merchants negotiating, the boy being inspected
panels.action: At a crowded Red Sea port, Arab and Indian traders bargain near moored ships while an Abyssinian youth is examined by a buyer before the voyage east.

dialogue.text: In this same ocean, Portuguese and others ran their own slave trades, but Chapu’s path led into Muslim hands and, eventually, toward India.

i18n.hi: इसी समुंदर में पुर्तगाली वगैरह भी ग़ुलाम बेचते थे, पर चापू की राह मुसलमान आक़ाओं तक गई, और फिर धीरे-धीरे हिंदुस्तान की तरफ।

panels.shot: mid-shot on a Deccan court interior, young Malik Ambar standing respectfully before an Ahmadnagar noble
panels.action: Inside a vaulted Deccan hall, a young Malik Ambar in simple but neat attire stands with lowered gaze before a seated Ahmadnagar noble who evaluates him.

dialogue.text: Sold again in the Deccan, the Abyssinian slave entered Ahmadnagar’s world of competing nobles, where military talent could lift a man even in chains.

i18n.hi: दक्खन में फिर से बेचा गया तो यह अबिस्सिनीय ग़ुलाम अहमदनगर के अमीरों की दुनिया में दाख़िल हुआ, जहां तलवार का हुनर ज़ंजीरों से भी ऊपर उठ सकता था।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Malik Ambar on horseback in training, dust clouds, Deccan fort in the background
panels.action: Malik Ambar, now in light armor, urges a horse through a cloud of dust near a hill fort, his eyes sharp as he practices with seasoned cavalrymen.

dialogue.text: He learned the Deccan’s hills and plains, its horses and men, until his master freed him, and the former bondman began to gather his own followers.

i18n.hi: उसने दक्खन के पहाड़, मैदानी राहें, घोड़े और लोग पहचाने, यहां तक कि मौक़ा मिलते ही उसके मालिक ने उसे आज़ाद कर दिया, और यह पूर्व ग़ुलाम अपने सिपाही जुटाने लगा।

panels.shot: tabletop strategy shot, overhead, showing Malik Ambar with a small band plotting routes across the Deccan
panels.action: By lamplight, Malik Ambar leans over a rough map scratched on cloth, gesturing across hill passes as a small band of loyal horsemen watch intently.

dialogue.text: Freed but never forgetting his bondage, Ambar built a troop of Abyssinians and Deccanis, selling their swords to survive the fracturing Bahmani world.

i18n.hi: आज़ाद हुआ, मगर बेड़ियों की याद कभी न भूली; अंबर ने अबिस्सिनीय और दक्खनी सवारों का दल बनाया, टूटती बहमनी दुनिया में तलवारें बेचकर गुज़र चलाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ahmadnagar fort under threat with Mughal banners in the distance and internal factions arguing in the courtyard
panels.action: Within Ahmadnagar’s strong stone walls, rival nobles argue heatedly as smoke rises in the distance where Mughal banners approach across the plains.

dialogue.text: By 1600, Ahmadnagar reeled under Mughal attack and court intrigue, its throne contested, its frontier eaten away by the empire of Akbar’s heirs.

i18n.hi: 1600 तक आते-आते अहमदनगर मुग़ल हमलों और दरबारी साज़िशों से डगमगा रहा था; तख़्त पर झगड़ा, सरहदें अकबर के वारिसों की सल्तनत निगल रही थी।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-wide inside a modest hall where Ambar presents a young prince, Murtaza Nizam Shah II, to loyalists
panels.action: In a modest but packed hall, Malik Ambar stands beside a veiled young prince, raising his arm toward the assembly of soldiers and nobles gathered.

dialogue.text: Ambar brought forward Murtaza Nizam Shah II as sultan, turning the boy into a symbol and the throne into a shield for Deccan resistance.

i18n.hi: अंबर ने मुर्तज़ा निज़ाम शाह द्वितीय को सामने लाकर सुल्तान बनाया, उस लड़के को निशान और तख़्त को दक्खनी मुकाबले की ढाल बना दिया।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot of Ambar seated behind the throne, the young sultan on it, courtiers watching
panels.action: The young Nizam Shah sits stiffly on an ornate throne while, just behind and to the side, Malik Ambar sits alert, issuing calm instructions to scribes and guards.

dialogue.text: In practice, the former slave became de facto ruler, steering Ahmadnagar’s policy, money and armies in the shadow of the child-king’s seat.

i18n.hi: असल हक़ीक़त में वही पूर्व ग़ुलाम असली शासक बन बैठा, बाल-राजा की आड़ में अहमदनगर की नीति, ख़ज़ाना और फ़ौजें सब अपनी मुट्ठी में चलाने लगा।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the founding of Khadki, with workers laying foundations, Ambar overseeing from a rise
panels.action: On an open plateau, laborers trace new streets with stakes and ropes as foundations are dug and Malik Ambar watches from a small rise, pointing toward the distant hills.

dialogue.text: He founded a new capital, Khadki near the future Aurangabad, to anchor his rule and better guard the routes across the Deccan.

i18n.hi: उसने नई रियासत बसाई—खड़की, जो आगे चलकर औरंगाबाद के पास बनी—ताकि अपनी हकूमत को थाम सके और दक्खन की राहों पर बेहतर नज़र रखे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of farmers and officials measuring fields with ropes and poles while Ambar observes
panels.action: In a rural scene, officials stretch ropes across a field, noting figures on palm leaves, as Malik Ambar watches a farmer demonstrate the soil in his hand.

dialogue.text: Omar H. Ali notes how Ambar ordered land measured and soils assessed, tightening revenue without trusting guesswork or purely noble claims.

i18n.hi: ओमर एच. अली लिखते हैं कि अंबर ने ज़मीन की पैमाइश करवाई, मिट्टी की जाँच करवाई, ताकि लगान अंदाज़े या सिर्फ़ अमीरों की बातों पर नहीं, ठोस हिसाब पर टिका रहे।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of mobile cavalry moving through rugged terrain, avoiding a larger distant Mughal camp
panels.action: A lean column of cavalry under Malik Ambar threads through rocky ravines, skirting a distant, sprawling Mughal camp pitched on the plain below.

dialogue.text: Against Mughal hosts, he avoided open battle, using swift horsemen to strike supply lines, harass camps and vanish into the plateau’s folds.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल फ़ौजों के सामने वह खुली लड़ाई से बचता, तेज़ सवारों से रसद काटता, डेरों को सताता और फिर पठार की दरारों में ग़ायब हो जाता।

panels.shot: close mid-shot of Ambar conferring with a Maratha commander like Shahaji Bhosale, maps between them
panels.action: Inside a field tent, Malik Ambar and a Maratha chief stand over a cloth map, fingers tracing hill paths while armored retainers wait outside.

dialogue.text: He worked with Maratha leaders such as Shahaji Bhosale, weaving local chiefs and Afghan and Abyssinian soldiers into a restless, mounted web.

i18n.hi: वह शाहाजी भोसले जैसे मराठा सरदारों के साथ काम करता, देसी मुखियाओं, अफ़ग़ान और अबिस्सिनीय घुड़सवारों को मिलाकर एक बेचैन, दौड़ती जाल बुनता।

panels.shot: wide battlefield shot showing Mughal army columns bogged down, while distant fires mark burning granaries
panels.action: Mughal infantry and elephants trudge through muddy terrain as smoke curls from burning granaries in the distance, tiny horsemen riding away along the skyline.

dialogue.text: By tearing at grain, water and pay, his tactics drained Mughal campaigns, forcing even the great empire to taste scarcity in unfamiliar lands.

i18n.hi: धान, पानी और तनख़्वाह पर वार करके उसकी चालों ने मुग़ल मुहिमों का ख़ून सुखा दिया, यहां तक कि इस बड़े साम्राज्य को भी अनजानी धरती पर भूख का स्वाद चखना पड़ा।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot of Jahangir in his court, angrily pointing at a painting or map of Ambar’s region
panels.action: In an opulent Mughal hall, Emperor Jahangir rises from his throne, his face tense as he gestures sharply toward a painted map of the Deccan hung nearby.

dialogue.text: In the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, the emperor cursed this ‘wretch of a slave’, recording his anger at a rebel who refused to submit.

i18n.hi: तज़्किरा तुज़ुक-ए-जहाँगीरी में बादशाह ने इस ‘कमबख़्त ग़ुलाम’ को कोसा, एक ऐसे बाग़ी पर अपना ग़ुस्सा लिख डाला जो झुकने से इनकार करता था।

panels.shot: close-up on Malik Ambar’s face, weathered and intent, by firelight in a campaign tent
panels.action: By flickering firelight inside a worn campaign tent, Malik Ambar’s lined face is shown in close-up, his gaze fixed, hands resting on a rolled map.

dialogue.speaker: malik_ambar
dialogue.text: No emperor owns these hills. We answer only to the land and our word.

i18n.hi: इन पहाड़ों पर किसी बादशाह की मिल्कियत नहीं। हमारा जवाब बस इस धरती और अपनी ज़ुबान को है।

panels.shot: somber mid-wide in Khadki, showing Malik Ambar older, supported slightly, watching troops drill below
panels.action: An older, slightly stooped Malik Ambar stands on a terrace in Khadki, hands on the parapet, observing disciplined troops drilling in the courtyard below.

dialogue.text: By the 1620s, he was aging, still campaigning yet weighed by years of war, revenue disputes and the fragile loyalties he had bound together.

i18n.hi: 1620 के दशक तक वह बूढ़ा हो चला था; अब भी लड़ाइयाँ करता, पर बरसों की जंग, लगान के झगड़े और नाज़ुक वफ़ादारियाँ उसके कंधों पर भारी पड़ने लगीं।

panels.shot: quiet interior shot of Ambar on a low bed, attendants around, city visible through a window
panels.action: Inside a modest but dignified chamber, Malik Ambar lies propped on a low bed as attendants stand silently by and the growing city of Khadki can be seen through a latticed window.

dialogue.text: Malik Ambar died in 1626, leaving a shaken Ahmadnagar and a Deccan still under pressure, his reforms and alliances tested without his will to hold them.

i18n.hi: मलिक अंबर 1626 में चल बसा; अहमदनगर हिल गया, दक्खन पर दबाव बना रहा, और उसके सुधारों व गठबंधनों की क़समत अब उसके बिना आज़माई जाने लगी।

panels.shot: epic wide of the Deccan plateau at sunset, ghostly superimposition of Malik Ambar’s figure fading into the landscape
panels.action: At sunset, the Deccan plateau stretches in rust and gold, with a faint, towering image of Malik Ambar’s figure dissolving into the hills and fields he once commanded.

dialogue.text: His life does not erase the violence of the chains that first carried him, but it shows how even a stolen child could bend empires and redraw the Deccan’s fate.

i18n.hi: उसकी ज़िंदगी उन ज़ंजीरों की हिंसा नहीं मिटाती जो उसे पहले बाँध कर लाईं, पर यह दिखाती है कि छिना हुआ एक बच्चा भी साम्राज्यों को मोड़ सकता है और दक्खन की तक़दीर नई लिख सकता है।

title_i18n.en: The Abyssinian Minister Who Would Not Yield
title_i18n.hi: अबिस्सिनीय मंत्री जिसने कभी घुटने नहीं टेके

subtitle_i18n.en: From Abyssinian Bondman to the Shadow on Jahangir’s Throne
subtitle_i18n.hi: अबिस्सिनीय ग़ुलाम से जहाँगीर की छाया तक
